definition: Translating sign-language video into spoken-language text, treating signing as a continuous visual sequence rather than static gestures.
details: Translating sign-language video into spoken-language text, treating signing as a continuous visual sequence rather than static gestures. It requires pose and hand-shape modeling and remains an open accessibility challenge.

explainer.lead: Sign language translation converts sign-language video into spoken-language text, treating signing as a continuous visual sequence rather than static gestures. It matters because it remains an open accessibility challenge.

tiers.eli5: It watches a whole video of someone signing and writes out what they mean in a spoken language.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers must model pose and hand shape over continuous sequences rather than isolated gestures. A pitfall is treating signing as a series of static gestures, which misses the continuous visual structure.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it maps sign-language video to spoken-language text as a continuous visual sequence, requiring pose and hand-shape modeling; it remains an open accessibility challenge.

explainer.example: A continuous video of a person signing is processed for pose and hand shape and output as spoken-language text.
